done.why: I saw the opening cavern, garden and gazebo, and stopped early without solving anything.

about: A cave-and-treasure exploration game in the Zork/Colossal Cave tradition. A meddling Wizard casts words that conjure or alter things, such as phantom objects or fear. Treasures lie south of a ravine.

moments.note: Jumping into the ravine summoned the Wizard, who explained where the treasures are.
The chest on the bridge was unreal because of the Wizard's spell. It was a clever but puzzling reveal.
Walking away made the room settle down and stop being odd.
The Wizard's Fear spell forced me out of the gazebo before I could take anything.

wished: Take things from the gazebo tea table.
Find the stone door that asks a question.
Get a hint of what the Wizard's words do.

lines.line: For a change, you look before leaping. You realize you would never survive.
lines.why: Dry humour in response to a contrary action.

lines.line: the room, having no say in the matter, let it, and has the grace to look embarrassed about it now.
lines.why: Charming way to say an item is a phantom.

fun.why: The Wizard's meddling is lively and the replies are witty.

engagement.why: Interesting hooks, but I left early.

difficulty.why: I did not get stuck, but did not attempt the puzzles.

interestingness.why: Phantom objects and spells give an unusual twist on a classic cave.

prose.why: Witty, polished narration that adds personality to a classic map.
